title: Reduce trace noise with content-aware prefilter and background commit
creator: Leila Chen
description: Problem: Host-level tracing is adding measurable CPU and allocation pressure on request hotpaths, raising p50/p95 CPU usage and occasionally increasing p99 latency under high QPS. Existing tail-based and probabilistic samplers retain valuable traces but rely on heavy span encoding and synchronous sample-commit on the request path. This ticket proposes a two-part approach: 1) a lightweight content-aware prefilter that makes a cheap, deterministic decision in the hotpath to tag low-value requests for downstream drop/low-priority sampling; 2) move span encoding and sample-commit to a background worker with backpressure-aware batching and retry, preserving tail-sampling guarantees while eliminating most hotpath allocations and locks.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU attributable to tracing reduced by >= 40% in synthetic 10k RPS benchmark compared to baseline
Median request allocation for instrumented service reduced by >= 30% with tracing enabled
No degradation in tail-sampling recall for incidents: maintain >= 95% recall for traces flagged as anomalous by existing detectors
End-to-end trace delivery success rate >= 99.5% for sampled traces across canary cluster under normal load
New instrumentation feature gated behind runtime flag and has integration tests + dashboard showing prefilter decisions
milestones: Prototype prefilter SDK hook and in-process tag (week 1): lightweight heuristics for path+status+size
Background commit worker (week 2): async span encoder, backpressure queue, metrics for backlog and drop counts
Perf harness and benchmark (week 3): run 3-node synthetic load with old vs new to measure CPU/allocs and p99 latency
Canary rollout (week 4): enable in 5% and 25% traffic windows with rollout playbook
Full rollout + retro (week 5): observe for 7 days, ship with release observability dashboard
implementation_notes: Prefilter heuristics designed to be deterministic and O(1): check HTTP route, response code ranges, request size, and presence of debug headers. Keep rule evaluation under 30ns on average.
Prefilter tags are simple byte flags on request context to avoid allocation; SDK exposes an inline function that returns a 1-byte decision code.
Background commit runs in a bounded MPSC queue per worker; use lock-free ring buffer where possible and fall back to a small mutex-protected queue if instrumentation not available on platform.
Span encoding moved to a reusable arena/string-builder to minimize per-span allocations; reuse buffers across requests with a safe epoch-based pool.
Introduce negotiated sample-ack protocol between agent and collector for durable delivery without blocking request path. Collector exposes backlog depth and ack-lag metrics for autoscaling signals.
Add e2e and unit tests: decision coverage for prefilter rules, queue overflow behaviour, and ack-based retry semantics. Add chaos test simulating collector flaps to ensure no unbounded memory growth.
Danger: overly aggressive prefiltering could remove rare but important failure signals. We'll run a conservative default rule set and collect false-negative telemetry during canary to tune rules.
risks: Loss of signal for rare errors if prefilter rules too aggressive
Background queue memory growth if collector outages are long and backpressure not enforced
Increased complexity in SDK surface may lead to inconsistent instrumentation across languages
Telemetry showing reduced spans may make some dashboards less informative until sampling config updated
dependencies: ENG-75910-sdk-cross-lang-generic-hooks (hotpath hook surface in other language SDKs)

2026-03-02 - SRE Review (Ava Martinez): SRE requested a kill-switch runtime flag and explicit backlog metrics. Added backlog_depth and ack_lag to implementation notes.

2026-03-06 - Marco Alvarez: Background commit worker prototype merged to feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821. Early bench shows 45% hotpath CPU reduction in synthetic test with 5k RPS.

2026-03-09 - Performance (Ravi Singh): End-to-end bench with 10k RPS shows allocations down 34% and no measurable p99 latency regression. Need to validate tail-sampling recall against historical incident data next.
